A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MVGS work. All 20 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables, references and Appendices A-F, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MVGS reconstruction experiments, quantitative and qualitative comparisons, component ablations and sensitivity analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark outcomes in Tables 1-4 and appendix experiments in Tables 5-9.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.4 retain the same multi-view regulated training, cross-intrinsic guidance, cross-ray densification and multi-view augmented densification procedures. No component, objective or algorithmic step changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks&Temples, Deep Blending, Shiny Blender, Glossy Synthetic, D-NeRF and BungeeNeRF for the same static, reflective, dynamic and multi-scale reconstruction tasks. Appendix scene coverage also matches.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within corresponding main-text and appendix experiments. The 3DGS, Scaffold-GS, 3DGS-DR, 4DGS and Octree-GS baselines, along with the other reported comparison methods, are retained.

E3.justification: Reported evaluation settings are unchanged, including PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics, the 800 x 800 rendering resolution in Table 3, and the view-count and training-iteration sweeps in Figures 5 and 7.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same component ablations, view-count sensitivity analysis, additional-training control and HDR/normal-map comparisons in Section 4.1 and Appendices A, B and D. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and curves without repeated-run counts, seed information, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1-9 and the figures retain the same numerical and qualitative results. For example, 3DGS with MVGS remains at 29.61 dB on Mip-NeRF 360 in Table 1, and 4DGS with MVGS remains at 35.11 dB and 102 FPS in Table 3.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, rendering and loss formulations, gradient aggregation and adaptive densification threshold in Equations 1-4 are unchanged. Neither version adds different assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same four contributions, broad applicability claims and claim of approximately 1 dB PSNR improvement across tasks.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and applicability interpretations are unchanged. Both retain Section 4.1's qualification that excessive training views can degrade performance through regional overfitting; no substantive limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: Section 3.5 retains the view settings {48, 24, 12, 8}, tau = 1 and reliance on baseline implementation settings. The abstract's code-access link has the same destination, and no reproducibility information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to NeRF, Gaussian splatting and methods using pretrained networks. No citation or novelty relationship changes.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv identifier/date changes from v1, 2 Oct 2024 to v2, 20 Sep 2025. Paper wording, terminology, section order and appendix organization otherwise match after accounting for extraction spacing.

P2.justification: Figures 1-12 and Tables 1-9 retain their content, captions, axes, legends, formatting and placement. Visual inspection confirms no figure, table or page-layout revision beyond the version-stamp update noted under P1.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations and reproducibility information are unchanged throughout the main paper and Appendices A-F. The updated version stamp and negligible rendering differences produce no meaningful improvement or deterioration in overall paper quality.
